profile.campus: Sterling, Loudoun County, Virginia (CyrusOne Northern Virginia campus, NVA5)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own official facility page, this NVA5 building (or campus) sits at 21350 Pacific Boulevard, Sterling, VA 20166 and publishes  of technical space and 116 MW of total IT capacity across the shared NVA5-NVA7 campus (not confirmed as this single building's individual figure) of technical space and 116 MW of total IT capacity across the shared NVA5-NVA7 campus. 

This facility is part of CyrusOne's broader Sterling, Virginia data center campus in Loudoun County, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn-area data center corridor described by industry press as the world's densest concentration of data center capacity. Wikipedia's entry on CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction; CyrusOne itself was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, was headquartered in Dallas, Texas, went public in 2013, and was taken private in November 2021/2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company in a deal valued at approximately $15 billion; the acquisition closed in March 2022 and CyrusOne is no longer an SEC filer for current-period results. The Sterling campus sits alongside separate NVA-numbered buildings tracked elsewhere in this registry (NVA1 through NVA9), reflecting a data center operator practice, also seen at Digital Realty, Equinix and QTS in this same corridor, of numbering sequential buildings on a shared or adjacent multi-parcel campus rather than giving each building an entirely distinct site name.

Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors has repeatedly cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a major share of the county's budget, while Dominion Energy, the region's dominant electric utility, has flagged data center demand growth in Northern Virginia as a primary driver of its own long-term transmission and generation planning; CyrusOne's Sterling campus draws power from this same regional grid alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and QTS in the same Ashburn-Sterling-Loudoun County corridor.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of total IT capacity across 1.18 million square feet of technical space. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, this translates to roughly 2,900 racks, though the operator publishes capacity in megawatts rather than rack count. The campus holds ISO 14001 and ISO 50001 certifications, qualifying it for environmental management and energy management operations. It is also designated an NWF Certified Wildlife Habitat.

In Virginia's published data center capacity, this campus ranks 24th by megawatts published. The state has 326 mapped data center facilities overall but only 23 publish capacity figures to operator spec pages, totaling 1,375 MW. This campus represents 8.4 percent of Virginia's published capacity, placing it in the upper tier of facilities with public specifications but not among the state's largest.

The capacity is published for the Sterling campus as a whole (NVA5-NVA7), not confirmed to this specific building's individual contribution. Virginia's total published capacity of 1,375 MW is distributed across only 23 facilities with disclosed figures, indicating that most of the state's mapped data center footprint operates without public capacity statements. Whether this campus can scale further or is constrained by local power delivery is not published.
